refusals.sshHostMissing: Give the address of the SSH server.
refusals.hostMissing: Give the address of the database.
refusals.notAHost: Enter a hostname or an IP address, without the rest of a URL.
refusals.pickTunnel: Pick the server to tunnel through.
refusals.pickJump: Pick the server to jump through.
refusals.connectionGone: That connection is not there any more.
refusals.passphraseAlone: Paste the private key this passphrase is for, or clear the passphrase.
refusals.tunnelNotYours: The server to tunnel through is not one of yours.
refusals.jumpNotYours: The server to jump through is not one of yours.
refusals.sshPassword: Enter the password for the SSH login.
refusals.sshKey: Paste the private key for the SSH login.
refusals.notYours: That database is not one you can open.
refusals.tunnelGone: The server this connection tunnels through is not one of yours any more.
refusals.sshIncomplete: This connection's SSH login is incomplete. Edit it and save it again.
refusals.jumpGone: The server this tunnel jumps through is not one of yours any more.
refusals.databaseGone: That database is not there any more.
refusals.objectStore: An object store is browsed from its Buckets panel, not as a database.
refusals.unpublished: This database runs on another server and is not published on a port, so Polaris cannot reach it from here. Publish it on a port from the database's own screen, then open it again.
refusals.unpublishedShort: Runs on another server and is not published on a port, so Polaris cannot reach it from here.
refusals.redisCluster: A Redis cluster spreads its keys over several masters, and the browser reads one server at a time, so it cannot open one.
refusals.noSuchName: There is nothing here by that name.
refusals.notEditable: Values in this kind of database are not edited from the grid.
refusals.redisOnly: Only a Redis key has a value to open.
refusals.noPrimaryKey: This table has no primary key, so there is no way to change one row of it without risking the others. Use the statement box.
refusals.primaryKeyColumn: That column is part of the primary key. Changing it moves the row, so it goes through the statement box.
refusals.rowUnknown: That row cannot be identified - the page it came from did not carry its whole primary key.
refusals.mongoEmpty: Type a command document, for example '{' find: "users", limit: 20 '}'.
refusals.mongoNotJson: That is not a command document. Mongo takes JSON here, for example '{' find: "users", filter: '{' active: true '}', limit: 20 '}' - with the field names quoted.
refusals.noColumns: That table has no columns to read.
refusals.noOrderColumn: No such column to order by.
refusals.keyGone: That key is not there any more.
refusals.generic: That did not work. Nothing was changed.
refusals.readOnly: This connection is read-only, and {what} would change the database. Turn read-only off on the connection if you meant to.
refusals.sshSignInJump: Polaris could not sign in to {target} over SSH through {jump}. Check the address, the user and the {secret}.
refusals.sshSignIn: Polaris could not sign in to {target} over SSH. Check the address, the user and the {secret}.
refusals.loginUnreadable: Polaris cannot read the login stored for {server}. Add that server again under Servers, then save this connection.
refusals.noHostKey: Polaris has no key on record to check {server} against, so it will not tunnel through it. Remove it under Servers and add it again, then save this connection.
refusals.tunnelFailed: Polaris could not open the SSH tunnel through {server}. Check that the server is up and that the login still works.
refusals.forwardProhibited: {server} does not allow port forwarding for this SSH login, so the database cannot be reached through it. Allow TCP forwarding for that user in the server's SSH settings.
refusals.forwardUnreachable: {server} could not reach the database at {address}. Check that the database is running and listening on that address.
refusals.keyChanged: {target} answered with a different SSH key than the one pinned for this connection, so nothing was sent to it. If that server was rebuilt, check the new key in the connection's settings and trust it there.
refusals.publicKey: That is a public key. Use the private key - the file without .pub.
refusals.notAKey: That is not a private key Polaris can read. Use an OpenSSH, PEM or PuTTY key.
refusals.keyLocked: This key is locked with a passphrase. Enter it below.
refusals.certIsKey: That file holds a private key. Use the certificate here.
refusals.notACert: That is not a PEM certificate.
refusals.notAPemKey: That is not a PEM private key.
refusals.pemKeyLocked: This key is locked with a passphrase. Save a copy without one and use that file.
refusals.clientKeyMissing: Add the key that goes with this certificate.
refusals.clientCertMissing: Add the certificate that goes with this key.
refusals.wrongPassphrase: That passphrase does not unlock this key.
refusals.keyUnsupported: Polaris cannot use this kind of key. Use an Ed25519, ECDSA or RSA key.
refusals.keyTooCostly: This key asks for more work to unlock than Polaris allows. Save it again with fewer KDF rounds (100 or less).
refusals.puttyV3: This PuTTY key is locked in PuTTY's newer format, which Polaris cannot unlock. In PuTTYgen, export it as an OpenSSH key, or save it with no passphrase, and use that file.
refusals.certUntrusted: The database's certificate is not signed by an authority this connection trusts, so nothing was sent to it. If its certificate was replaced, check it in the connection's settings.
refusals.certExpired: The database's certificate has expired or is not valid yet, so nothing was sent to it.
refusals.noTls: This database server does not accept encrypted connections. Turn encryption off for it, or turn TLS on at the server.
refusals.noRoot: The server's certificate is signed by an authority it does not send, so there is nothing to trust on first use. Upload that authority's certificate instead.
refusals.passwordAgain: Enter the password again. The address changed, and a saved password is only sent to the address it was saved for.
refusals.passwordAgainTls: Enter the password again. The encryption is weaker now, and a saved password is only sent over a connection as safe as the one it was saved for.
refusals.sshSecretAgain: Enter the SSH password or key again. The SSH server changed, and a saved login is only sent to the server it was saved for.
refusals.caMissing: Upload the certificate of the authority that signed the server's certificate.
refusals.caInvalid: That certificate file could not be read. Use a PEM file with one or more certificates.
refusals.clientMissing: Add the client certificate and its key.
refusals.clientInvalid: That client certificate and key could not be read, or do not belong together.
refusals.keyChangedAgain: The server's key changed again since you checked it. Check it again before trusting it.
refusals.certChangedAgain: The server's certificate changed again since you checked it. Check it again before trusting it.
refusals.notTofu: This connection does not trust the server's own certificate, so there is nothing to check.
refusals.notManualTunnel: This connection has no SSH login of its own to check.
refusals.secretUnreadable: The saved password could not be read. Enter it again.
refusals.jumpKeyChanged: {server} answered with a different SSH key than the one Polaris has on record for it, so nothing was sent to it. Check that server under Servers.
refusals.keyUnreachable: Polaris could not reach {target} to read its key. Check that the server is up.
refusals.certUnreachable: Polaris could not reach {target} to read its certificate.
refusals.certWrongName: The database's certificate is not for {host}, so nothing was sent to it.
refusals.egressForbidden: Polaris does not connect to {host}: it is a link-local or metadata address, which never holds a database.
refusals.egressInternal: {host} is on a private network, which only an administrator can reach from Polaris. Reach it over SSH through a server of yours instead.
refusals.egressUnresolved: Polaris could not find {host}. Check the name.
refusals.tooManyAttempts: Too many connection attempts. Try again in {seconds} s.
refusals.tableName: A table name starts with a letter or an underscore and holds only letters, digits and underscores.
refusals.columnNameRule: A column name starts with a letter or an underscore and holds only letters, digits and underscores.
refusals.columnName: "{column}" cannot be a column name: letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter.
refusals.autoKey: {column} is numbered automatically, so it has to be the primary key.
refusals.autoDefault: {column} is numbered automatically and takes no default.
refusals.unknownDefault: That default is not one Polaris offers.
refusals.defaultType: That default does not fit the type of {column}.
refusals.defaultTooLong: A default can be at most 200 characters.
refusals.defaultBackslash: A default cannot hold a backslash or a line break.
refusals.defaultNumber: That default has to be a number.
refusals.defaultBoolean: A yes/no column takes true or false as its default.
refusals.noPrimaryKeyDelete: This table has no primary key, so there is no way to remove one row of it without risking the others. Use the statement box.
refusals.tooManyRows: Remove at most 200 rows at a time from here.
refusals.tooManyColumns: A table made here can have at most 100 columns.
refusals.noColumnsGiven: Give the table at least one column.
refusals.noRowWrites: Rows in this kind of database are not added or removed from the grid.
refusals.noCreateTable: Tables in this kind of database are not created from here.
refusals.notShipped: This server does not ship that extension.
refusals.notInstalled: That extension is not installed here.
refusals.keptExtension: That extension is part of the database and stays.
refusals.statsPostgresOnly: Query statistics are recorded by PostgreSQL only.
refusals.statsHosted: This database lives inside another instance; turn statistics on for that instance.
refusals.deployFirst: Deploy this database first - it has no container yet.
refusals.putBack: The instance did not start that way, so it was put back: {reason}
refusals.objectStoreKeys: An object store's keys are managed from its Buckets panel.
refusals.severalContainers: This instance runs as several containers, and their passwords are changed together by redeploying it, not from here.
refusals.publishHosted: This database lives inside another instance; publish that instance instead.
refusals.portServices: Ports 20000 to 39999 are kept for services. Pick another.
refusals.portTaken: Another database on this server already uses that port.
refusals.publicPutBack: The database did not start that way, so it was put back: {reason}

dialog.intro: A database Polaris runs, or one somewhere else you have the credentials for.
dialog.name: Name
dialog.noManaged: Polaris is not running any databases yet.
dialog.unreachable: This one runs on another server and is not published on a port, so Polaris cannot reach it from here. Publish it on a port from the database's own screen first.
dialog.hostHint: As the SSH server sees it - usually 127.0.0.1.
dialog.keepSaved: Leave empty to keep the saved one.
dialog.sshHint: For a database that is not published on the network: Polaris signs in to a server that can see it and forwards the port.
dialog.noServers: No servers are connected yet. Add one under Servers, or use another login here.
dialog.serverGone: The server this connection tunneled through was removed from Servers. Pick another.
dialog.sshPasswordHint: Needed to sign in to the SSH server.
dialog.privateKeyHint: Paste it, drop the file here, or choose it. OpenSSH, PEM or PuTTY.
dialog.passphraseHint: The key is locked. This unlocks it.
dialog.jumpGone: The server this tunnel jumped through was removed from Servers. Pick another, or reach it straight.
dialog.jumpHint: A server Polaris already has, used to reach that SSH host.
dialog.hostKeyNote: The SSH server's key is remembered when this is saved, and checked on every connection after.
dialog.readOnlyHint: Refuses anything that would change the database. Turn it on for a database you came here to read.
dialog.passwordAgain: The address changed, so enter the password again.
dialog.passwordAgainTls: The encryption is weaker now, so enter the password again.
dialog.tlsUnverified: Nothing checks who answers, so someone on the network can read and change what is sent. Use a verify mode if you can.
dialog.tlsLegacy: Saved when encryption did not check the certificate. Pick a verify mode to close that gap.
dialog.tlsServerNote: Polaris reads the server's certificate when you save, and refuses any other after that. For a self-signed server.
dialog.clientCertHint: For a server that asks the client to prove who it is.
dialog.fileUnreadable: That file could not be read.
dialog.savedFile: Saved: {what}. Give a new one to replace it.
dialog.filePlaceholder: Paste it or drop the file here
dialog.keySame: The server still presents this key.
dialog.keyTrusted: New key trusted. Connections use it from now on.
dialog.keyDifferent: The server now presents a different key:

dialog.certSame: The server still presents this certificate.
dialog.certDifferent: The server now presents a different certificate:
dialog.sslHint: Encrypts what travels between Polaris and the database.

require.label: Encrypt only
require.hint: Nobody can read it on the way, but Polaris does not check who answers. For a server with its own certificate on a network you trust.

verify-ca.label: Check the certificate
verify-ca.hint: The certificate must be signed by an authority you trust. The name is not checked, so it suits a server reached by IP.

verify-full.label: Check the certificate and the name
verify-full.hint: The safest: signed by an authority you trust and issued for this exact address.

url.label: Connection URL
url.hint: Paste one to fill in the fields below. The URL itself is not kept.
url.filled: Filled in from the URL. Check the fields and save.
url.softened: It allowed an unencrypted fallback, so SSL is on without checking the certificate.

refusals.unreadable: That URL could not be read.
refusals.scheme: Use a URL that starts with postgres://, mysql://, mariadb://, mongodb:// or redis://.
refusals.srv: A mongodb+srv:// address is an SRV record, not a server. Use the plain mongodb:// one your provider also gives.
refusals.multihost: This URL lists several servers. Use the address of one of them, the primary if there is one.

dialog.noServersManual: No servers in Polaris yet, so sign in to the SSH server here.

notes.polaris: Read-only. Polaris itself runs on this one.
notes.tunnelRemoved: The server this connection tunnels through was removed from Servers. Edit it to pick another.
notes.jumpRemoved: The server this tunnel jumps through was removed from Servers. Edit it to pick another.

view.searchPlaceholder: Search by name, host or database
view.emptyBody: Polaris is not running a database for you, and none has been added. Point one at any PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, MongoDB or Redis you have the credentials for.
view.removeBody: The connection goes; the database itself is untouched.

stats.first: Taking the first reading. A rate is the difference between two, so the charts appear a moment after this one.
stats.hitRateHint: Hit rate - how much of what was asked for was already in memory

insights.noPgStatStatements: Postgres only records this with the pg_stat_statements extension installed. Ask whoever runs this database to add it.
insights.noPerformanceSchema: This server does not have the performance schema turned on, so it is not recording which statements run.
insights.biggestNote: Table, indexes and out-of-line storage together - what the table actually costs.
insights.frequentNote: Counted by the engine since it last started, with the values already stripped out.

bench.readOnly: Read-only. Nothing here can change the database.
bench.pick: Pick something on the left to see what is in it.
bench.rowGone: Nothing was changed - that row is no longer there.
bench.cannotRead: Polaris cannot read a {type} yet. Its type and expiry are above.
